answer.rationale: Promotional pricing (exp_73, memory_73) shows -12% 30-day retention and poor cohort survival—directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue, and would worsen churn velocity in a competitive price war. Referral incentives work well for *established* customers (memory_57), but are misaligned to the immediate SMB churn crisis. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is high-value but cannot address SMB churn at scale quickly. Activation messaging (memory_91) and simplified onboarding (memory_86, memory_31) are proven, retention-positive levers: messaging lifted week-one engagement, onboarding shortened time-to-value (+3% retention). A standard experiment pairing activation messaging with existing simplified onboarding can address the root problem—lack of perceived value driving price sensitivity—rather than competing on price. This preserves margin, aligns with sustainable growth mandate, and leverages confirmed low-risk mechanisms. The doubled churn conversations signal an urgency window; a broad rollout risks over-investing before SMB-specific messaging is validated, but a small test risks missing the moment.
